blockingIssues.description: Dead code branch in framework override logic (line 191): the ternary expression `ctx.testFramework && ctx.testFramework.length > 0 ? await detectTestFramework(ctx.repoRoot) : await detectTestFramework(ctx.repoRoot)` always calls detectTestFramework regardless of whether a testFramework override is provided. Both branches are identical. When an override IS provided, lines 197-200 replace only the framework name with the override, keeping the detected framework's language and testCommand — producing a mismatch (e.g., testFramework='vitest' detected as jest gives {name: 'vitest', testCommand: 'npx jest'}). The test for this case passes only because it doesn't verify testCommand consistency.

nonBlockingIssues.description: Unused type imports: ExecuteWorkstream and PlanItem are imported but never referenced.

PromptBuildContext.testFramework is typed as required string but semantics suggest it should be optional (testFramework?: string). IntegrateCommandOptions correctly uses optional, but PromptBuildContext does not.

extractGoal uses lossy type assertions (planArtifact.carry_forward as { task_spec?: { goal?: string } } | undefined) when PlanArtifactCarryForward is well-typed with required task_spec. Also accesses purpose via (planArtifact as { purpose?: string }).purpose when purpose IS a real property on PlanArtifact.

Bug in parseTestOutput generic fallback regex: genericFailed[2] ?? genericFailed[1] references capture group 2 from a regex that only has one capturing group. genericFailed[2] is always undefined, so nullish coalescing always falls through to genericFailed[1]. Produces correct result but code is misleading.

Path traversal concern: path.resolve(repoRoot, tf.path) does not validate that the resolved path stays within repoRoot. A malicious tf.path like '../../etc/passwd' would write outside the repo. Consistent with prompt-builder.ts pattern. Low risk since paths come from AI-generated content, but worth adding defense-in-depth check.

Success logic (runError === undefined && failed === 0 && total > 0) means unparseable output (total=0) yields success: false even if command ran without error. Reasonable design choice but worth documenting.
